newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN
National soccer league club the Collingwood Warriors served players with a letter of demand on Monday night to continue playing for the club or face legal action. Page 18.

Australian runner Dean Capobianco is focused on defending his national 200m title at the national championships in Melbourne next week before defending himself against the positive drug test for steroids at an International Amateur Athletic Federation heaing on March 15-16. Page 17

Sydney Flames point guard Annie La Fleur has been recalled to replace injured rookie guard Narelle Henry in the Australian Opals basketball squad in training camp in Canberra next week. Australia is playing a four game series against Japan in April, a fie game series against Russia or Spain in May and the Oceania world championship qualifying series against New Zealand in June. Page 17
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Rugby Union clubs are concerned that early kick-off times for first-grade matches will reduce match attendance's. Matches will begin an hour or 90 minutes early to ensure free-to air and pay television coverage does not coincide. Page 54

The Australian Rugby League lodged an application for an injunction in the Equity Division of the New South Wales Supreme Court yesterday, to prevent Canterbury's Jack Elsegood and Penrith's John Cross playing in rival competition Super League. Page 53

Adelaide City midfielder Angelo Costanzo suffered a setback in his recovery from a potentially permanent eye injury yesterday, requiring a third operation to stop the bleeding. Costanzo was struck in the left eye by a piece of broken glass after the Adelade City team bus was stoned by South Melbourne fans on Sunday night. Page 53.
THE AGE

Dual Olympic hurdles champion Roger Kingdom believes Australian champion Kyle Vander-Kuyp has the potential to win the 110 metres race at the Sydney Olympic Games. Kingdom was defeated by Vander-Kuyp in the preliminary rounds of the 1995 world championshis. Page C14

Horse trainer Peter Hayes will fit blinkers for the first time on filly Lady of The Pines in the 1200 metre Blue Diamond Stakes this Saturday. Both Lady of the Pines and pre-race favourite Schubert were impressive in their workouts at Caulfield yesterday sing the blinkers. Page C14

Australia defended a 353 run-lead in the fourth innings of their tour match against Western Province in Cape Town, South Africa, to win by 32 runs. Michael Bevan's bowling was a key factor in the win, with the left-arm wrist spinner taking three wickets fr 113 runs. Page C14
THE HERALD SUN

The Australian Football League will investigate suggestions the Sydney Swans tampered with the pre-season draft by negotiating with former Adelaide captain Tony McGuiness. McGuiness says he had a written agreement from Sydney to draft him - breaching the eague rules that prohibit players and clubs making pre-draft arrangements. Page 80
Australian cricket team captain Mark Taylor has denied allegations of racist behaviour and physical intimidation on the field from Sri Lankan captain Arjuna Ranatunga. Page 78

Soccer Australia is expected to throw the book at South Melbourne sweeper Alex Kuzmanovic and his club following Sunday's riot against Adelaide City. Kuzmanovic was yesterday given an automatic two match suspension and faces further charges for his part n the riot which ended with Adelaide City's Angelo Costanzo in hospital. Page 71
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian Rugby League captain Brad Fittler believes this year's State of Origin series will lose much of its credibility with Queensland's best players otherwise engaged in the rival Super League tri-series. Page 76

The venue for the final of Australia's one-day domestic cricket competition, the Mercantile Mutual Cup, is likely to be decided in an off-field battle. The major sponsor, Mercantile Mutual, wants the final to be played at North Sydney Oval while the Cricket Association and the players want the final at the Sydney Cricket Ground, if the New South Wales team beats Queensland in this weekend's semi-final match. Page 72
